Definition: properly, to twist or whirl (in a circular or spiral manner), i.e. (specifically) to dance, to writhe in pain (especially of parturition) or fear; figuratively, to wait, to pervert
BiblicalUsage: To wait is to stay in place until the time comes, and Noah waits seven more days before he sends the dove out again. The nations will tremble when they hear of Israel, and a woman in labour writhes before she brings forth. Saul is sorely wounded by the archers, and the same word that means waiting also means writhing in pain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe waiting and writhing belong to the same word because waiting in Scripture is never passive. Noah waits and watches, the nations tremble and wait, and the woman labours toward a birth. My position is that God uses waiting to do His deepest work, and the pain of it is often the sign that something is being born.
